cm.hebrew: אין ב"ד יכולים למנות אפוטרופוס להאמינו בלא שבועה אא"כ אינם מוצאים אדם הגון שירצה להיות אפוטרופוס אם לא יאמינוהו בלא שבועה דאז בהכרח ממנים מי שהגון לכך ופוטרים אותו משבועה ומ"מ קבלה סתם אומרים הב"ד דהא אין אומרים נגדו מפורש ולא יקפיד [נ"ל] וכשמשביעין אפוטרופוס שבועה בנק"ח שהיא שבועת המשנה צריך שיטענו אותו לפחות שתי כסף ופרוטה ויכפור בשתי כסף ויודה בפרוטה כדין שבועת התורה שנתבאר בסי' פ"ח וכמ"ש בסי' צ"ג בכל שבועות ספק אבל אם לא היתה טענה או כפירה והודאה כשיעור זה אם טוענין אותו טענת ודאי נשבע היסת כבכל טענות דעלמא ומגלגל עליו שלא עיכב בידו משלו כלום:

MINIMAL.translation: A beit din cannot appoint an apotropus to be trusted without an oath unless they cannot find a decent person who is willing to be an apotropus if they do not trust him without an oath; for then, by necessity, they appoint one who is decent for this and exempt him from an oath. Nevertheless, for a standard acceptance, the beit din speaks, as they do not speak explicitly against him and he will not be particular [it appears to me]. And when they administer an oath to an apotropus with a sacred object, which is the oath of the Mishnah, they must claim against him at least two kesef and a perutah, and he must deny two kesef and admit to a perutah, according to the law of a Torah oath as was explained in siman 88 and as I wrote in siman 93 regarding all oaths of doubt. But if there was no claim or denial and admission of this measure, if they claim against him a certain claim, he swears a hesset oath as with all general claims, and they include through gilgul that he did not withhold anything of theirs in his possession.

LOW.translation: A beit din cannot appoint an apotropus to be trusted without an oath unless they cannot find a decent person who would be willing to be an apotropus if they do not trust him without an oath, for then, out of necessity, they appoint someone who is fit for it and exempt him from an oath. Nevertheless, for a standard acceptance, the beit din speaks, for they do not speak explicitly against him and he will not be particular [it seems to me]. And when they administer an oath to an apotropus with a sacred object, which is the oath of the Mishnah, they must claim against him at least two silver ma'ah and a perutah, and he must deny two silver ma'ah and admit to a perutah, according to the law of a Torah oath as explained in siman 88 and as written in siman 93 regarding all oaths of doubt. But if there was no claim or denial and admission of this amount, if they claim against him a certain claim, he swears a hesset oath as with all general claims, and they include through gilgul that he did not withhold anything of theirs in his possession.

MEDIUM.translation: A beit din cannot appoint an apotropos to trust him without an oath unless they do not find a worthy person who wants to be an apotropos if they do not trust him without an oath, for then, out of necessity, they appoint someone who is worthy for this and exempt him from an oath. And nevertheless, the beit din says a general acceptance, for they do not say it explicitly against him and he will not be particular [it seems to me]. And when they administer an oath to an apotropos with the holding of a sacred object, which is the oath of the Mishnah, it is necessary that they claim against him at least two silver and a perutah, and he denies the two silver and admits to the perutah, according to the law of a Torah oath that was explained in siman 88, and as written in siman 93 regarding all oaths of doubt. But if there was no claim or denial and admission of this amount, if they claim against him a certain claim, he swears a shevuat hesset as with all general claims, and rolls upon him that he did not withhold anything of his in his hand.

HIGH.translation: Beit din cannot appoint an apotropos to trust him without an oath unless they do not find a worthy person who will agree to be an apotropos if they do not trust him without an oath, for then, out of necessity, they appoint one who is worthy for this and exempt him from an oath. And nevertheless, the beit din says a general acceptance, for they do not say it explicitly against him, and he will not object [it seems to me]. And when they administer an oath to an apotropos with a sacred object, which is the oath of the Mishnah, it is necessary that they claim against him at least two kesef and a perutah, and he denies two kesef and admits to a perutah, according to the law of a Torah oath that was explained in siman 88, and as was written in siman 93 regarding all oaths of doubt. But if there was no claim or denial and admission of this amount, if they claim against him a certain claim, he swears a hesset oath as with all general claims, and rolls upon him that he did not withhold anything of his in his hand.

cm.hebrew: מהיכן מודדין האמות מהעיקר הרחב של האילנות שהוא מקום יציאת האילן מן הארץ שהיא עבה ואם האילנות עומדים כסגול או שהיו מקורבים פחות מד"א או מרוחקים יותר מט"ז או שלקחן זה אחר זה או שמכר לו שנים בשדהו ואחד על המצר או שנים בתוך שלו ואחד בתוך של חבירו כגון שיש לו שני אילנות בקצה שדהו ויש לו עוד אילן אחד שקנה בשדה חבירו הסמוכה להן עם הקרקע ומכר אלו השלשה לאחד [רשב"ם] או שיש הפסק בור או אמת המים או רה"ר בין האילנות הרי זה אין לו קרקע וכן כשהפסיק ביניהם הרכבת דקלים הרבה [גמ'] לא קנה הקרקע ובכל אלו לבד כשאין עומדים כסגול בעיא היא בגמ' ולא איפשיטא וכל ספק מוקמינן בחזקת המוכר ותפיסה לא מהני בקרקע שתמיד עומדת בחזקת בעלים הראשונים [הה"מ] ואפי' אם נטען הלוקח לאחר שיבשו ואכל הפירות מוציאין מידו אפי' לדעת הפוסקים דמהני תפיסא בספיקא דדינא דכיון דבאילנות אין לו תפיסה ממילא דהפירות ברשות המוכר הן [נ"ל] ובכל אלו לא קנה גם האילנות הקטנות שביניהן ואם יבשו האילנות או נקצצו ילך לו ובכל מקום שנתבאר שאם יבשו האילנות אין לו ליטע אחרים תחתיהן זהו דווקא כשנקצצו ואין גזען מחליף וצריך ליטע אחרים אבל אם גזעו מחליף אין זה אילן חדש אלא כעולה מן הגזע דמי ושייך לבעל האילן:

MINIMAL.translation: From where do they measure the amot? From the wide base of the trees, which is the place where the tree emerges from the earth, which is thick. And if the trees stand like a segol, or if they were closer than four amot or further than sixteen, or if he bought them one after another, or if he sold him two in his field and one on the border, or two within his own and one within his fellow's—for example, if he has two trees at the edge of his field and he has one more tree that he bought in his fellow's field adjacent to them along with the ground, and he sold these three to one person [Rashbam]—or if there is an interruption of a pit or a water channel or a public domain between the trees, behold, this person does not have ground. And similarly, when a grafting of many palms interrupted between them [Gemara], he did not acquire the ground. And in all of these, except for when they do not stand like a segol, it is an inquiry in the Gemara and was not resolved, and every doubt we establish in the possession of the seller; and seizing does not avail regarding ground, which always stands in the possession of the original owners [Maggid Mishneh]. And even if the buyer claims after they dried up and he ate the fruits, they remove it from his hand even according to the opinion of the poskim that seizing avails in a legal doubt, for since regarding the trees he has no seizing, automatically the fruits are in the domain of the seller [it appears to me]. And in all of these, he also did not acquire the small trees that are between them, and if the trees dried up or were cut down, he must go away. And in every place where it was explained that if the trees dried up he may not plant others in their place, this is specifically when they were cut down and their trunk does not regrow and he must plant others; but if its trunk regrows, this is not a new tree, but rather it is considered as rising from the trunk and belongs to the owner of the tree.

LOW.translation: From where do we measure the cubits? From the wide base of the trees, which is the place where the tree emerges from the earth, which is thick. And if the trees stand in a triangle, or if they were closer than four cubits or further than sixteen, or if he bought them one after another, or if he sold him two in his field and one on the border, or two within his own and one within his fellow's—for example, if he has two trees at the edge of his field and he has another tree that he bought in his fellow's field adjacent to them with the land, and he sold these three to one person [Rashbam]—or if there is an interruption of a pit or a water channel or a public domain between the trees, behold, this person does not have land. And similarly, when a graft of many palms interrupted between them [Gemara], he did not acquire the land. And in all of these, except for when they do not stand in a triangle, it is an inquiry in the Gemara and was not resolved, and every doubt we establish in the possession of the seller; and seizing does not avail regarding land, which always remains in the possession of the original owners [Maggid Mishneh]. And even if the buyer claims after they dried up and he ate the fruits, we remove them from his hand, even according to the opinion of the poskim that seizing avails in a legal doubt, for since regarding the trees he has no seizing, automatically the fruits are in the domain of the seller [it appears to me]. And in all of these, he also did not acquire the small trees that are between them, and if the trees dried up or were cut down, he must go. And in every place where it was explained that if the trees dried up he may not plant others in their place, this is specifically when they were cut down and their trunk does not grow back and he needs to plant others, but if its trunk grows back, this is not a new tree, but rather it is considered as rising from the trunk and belongs to the owner of the tree.

MEDIUM.translation: From where do we measure the amot? From the wide base of the trees, which is the place where the tree emerges from the earth, which is thick. And if the trees stand as a segol, or if they were closer than four amot or further than sixteen, or if he bought them one after the other, or if he sold him two in his field and one on the metzar, or two within his own and one within his fellow's—for example, he has two trees at the edge of his field and he has one more tree that he bought in his fellow's field adjacent to them with the land, and he sold these three to one [the Rashbam]—or if there is an interruption of a pit or a water channel or a reshut harabim between the trees, behold, this one does not have land. And likewise, when a row of many palms interrupted between them [Gemara], he did not acquire the land. And in all these, except for when they do not stand as a segol, it is an inquiry in the Gemara and was not resolved; and every doubt we establish in the presumption of the seller, and tefisa is not effective regarding land, which always stands in the presumption of the first owners [the Maggid Mishneh]. And even if the buyer claims after they dried up and he ate the fruits, we remove from his hand, even according to the opinion of the poskim that tefisa is effective in a safeka de-dina; for since regarding the trees he has no tefisa, automatically the fruits are in the domain of the seller [it appears to me]. And in all these, he also did not acquire the small trees that are between them; and if the trees dried up or were cut down, he must go. And in every place where it was explained that if the trees dried up he may not plant others in their place, this is specifically when they were cut down and their stump does not regenerate and he needs to plant others; but if its stump regenerates, this is not a new tree, but rather it is considered as rising from the stump and belongs to the owner of the tree.

HIGH.translation: From where do we measure the cubits? From the wide base of the trees, which is the place where the tree emerges from the earth, which is thick. And if the trees stand like a segol, or if they were closer than four cubits or further than sixteen, or if he purchased them one after another, or if he sold him two in his field and one on the boundary, or two within his own and one within his fellow's—for example, if he has two trees at the edge of his field and he has another tree that he bought in his fellow's field adjacent to them with the land, and he sold these three to one [Rashbam]—or if there is an interruption of a pit or a water channel or a public domain between the trees, behold, this [person] has no land. And similarly, when a row of many palm trees interrupted between them [Gemara], he did not acquire the land. And in all these, except when they do not stand like a segol, it is an inquiry in the Gemara and it was not resolved. And every doubt we establish in the possession of the seller, and seizing does not avail regarding land, which always stands in the possession of the first owners [the Maggid Mishneh]. And even if the buyer claims after they dried up and he ate the fruits, we remove [them] from his hand, even according to the opinion of the poskim that seizing avails in a legal doubt, for since regarding the trees he has no seizure, automatically the fruits are in the domain of the seller [it appears to me]. And in all these, he also did not acquire the small trees that are between them. And if the trees dried up or were cut down, he shall go his way. And in every place where it was explained that if the trees dried up he may not plant others in their place, this is specifically when they were cut down and their trunk does not regenerate and he must plant others; but if its trunk regenerates, this is not a new tree, but rather it is considered as rising from the trunk and belongs to the owner of the tree.

cm.hebrew: שכר סתם ונפל בית המשכיר שהיה דר בו ואין לו בית אחר זולת בית השוכר ה"ז יכול להוציא את השוכר מביתו אף בלא הודעה ל' יום מקודם ואף בימות הגשמים דאומר לו אינו בדין שתהיה אתה יושב בביתי עד שתמצא מקום ואני אהיה מושלך ברחוב הרי לא שכרת לזמן ואין אתה בעל זכות בביתי מפני שאתה דר בה יותר ממני וההודעה אינה אלא כדי למצא דירה וממילא כיון שביתי היא הנני בעל זכות בה יותר ממך [עי' בש"ע סעיף י"א ודוק] ודוקא בשכר סתם אבל בשוכר לזמן ידוע אינו יכול להוציאו תוך הזמן כמ"ש דעל הזמן הזה הוה כשלו ממש ויש להסתפק בחנות בשכר סתם ונפלה חנותו של המשכיר אם יכול להוציאו כיון שלהשוכר יש בזה הפסד חובות ולהמשכיר אין נ"מ אם יתיישב בחנות זה או בחנות אחר כיון שלא ישב בה מקודם ונראה שאינו יכול להוציאו:

MINIMAL.translation: If one rented without a specified term and the house of the lessor where he was living fell, and he has no other house besides the house of the lessee, he may evict the lessee from his house even without thirty days' prior notice and even during the rainy season. For he says to him: It is not right that you should sit in my house until you find a place while I am cast out in the street; behold, you did not rent for a set time, and you are not a holder of a right in my house such that you should dwell in it more than I, and the notice is only so that one may find an apartment, and automatically since it is my house, I am the holder of the right in it more than you [see in the Shulchan Aruch, seif 11, and examine carefully]. And this is specifically when he rented without a specified term, but if he rented for a known time, he cannot evict him within the time, as has been written, for during this time it is like his own. And there is a doubt regarding a shop rented without a specified term where the shop of the lessor fell, whether he can evict him, since for the lessee there is a loss of debts in this, and for the lessor there is no difference whether he settles in this shop or in another shop since he did not sit in it previously; and it appears that he cannot evict him.

LOW.translation: If one rented without a specified term and the house of the lessor where he was living fell, and he has no other house besides the house of the lessee, he may remove the lessee from his house even without thirty days' prior notice and even during the rainy season, for he says to him: It is not right that you should sit in my house until you find a place while I am cast out in the street; behold, you did not rent for a set time and you are not a possessor of rights in my house such that you should dwell in it more than I, and the notice is only in order to find an apartment, and automatically, since it is my house, I am the possessor of rights in it more than you [see in the Shulchan Aruch, seif 11, and examine closely]. And this is specifically when he rented without a specified term, but in the case of one who rents for a known time, he cannot remove him within the time, as I have written, for regarding this time it is like his very own. And there is a doubt regarding a shop rented without a specified term where the shop of the lessor fell, whether he can remove him, since for the lessee there is a loss of debts in this, and for the lessor there is no difference whether he settles in this shop or in another shop since he did not sit in it previously, and it appears that he cannot remove him.

MEDIUM.translation: [If one] rented without a specified term and the house of the landlord in which he was living fell, and he has no other house except for the house of the renter, behold, he is able to evict the renter from his house even without thirty days' prior notice and even during the rainy season, for he says to him: It is not right that you should be sitting in my house until you find a place, while I am cast out in the street. Behold, you did not rent for a [fixed] time, and you are not a holder of a right in my house because you live in it more than I [do], and the notice is only in order to find a dwelling; and automatically, since it is my house, I am the holder of a right in it more than you [see in the Shulchan Aruch, seif 11, and examine closely]. And specifically in [a case where] he rented without a specified term, but in [a case of] one who rents for a known time, he cannot evict him within the time, as has been written, for regarding this time, it is like his own property. And there is a doubt regarding a shop [rented] without a specified term and the landlord's shop fell, whether he can evict him, since for the renter there is in this a loss of debts, and for the landlord there is no difference if he settles in this shop or in another shop, since he did not sit in it previously; and it appears that he cannot evict him.

HIGH.translation: One who rented without a fixed term and the landlord's house in which he was living collapsed, and he has no other house besides the tenant's house, behold, he may evict the tenant from his house even without thirty days' prior notice and even during the rainy season, for he says to him: It is not right that you should sit in my house until you find a place while I am cast out into the street; behold, you did not rent for a fixed time and you are not the holder of a right in my house because you live in it more than I, and the notice is only in order to find a dwelling, and consequently, since it is my house, I am the holder of a right in it more than you [see Shulchan Aruch, seif 11, and examine carefully]. And specifically in a case of renting without a fixed term, but in a case of renting for a known time, he cannot evict him within the time, as has been written, for during this time it is like his very own. And there is a doubt regarding a shop rented without a fixed term and the landlord's shop collapsed, whether he can evict him, since for the tenant there is a loss of debts in this, and for the landlord there is no difference whether he settles in this shop or in another shop since he did not sit in it previously, and it appears that he cannot evict him.
